title: Cyril of Jerusalem on 1 Kings 1:4
body: “Cyril's argument is fully justified by the actual usage of "Almah," which certainly refers to unmarried women in Gen.”
author: Cyril of Jerusalem, Catechetical Lectures

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Kings 8:39
body: “The meaning is of this kind. "He who dwells in men's hearts, and enters into their thoughts, took no heed of outward words; and knowing well that their warmth was but for a season, He placed not confidence in them as in perfect disciples, nor committed all His doctrines to them as though they had already become firm believers." Now, to know what is in the heart of men belongs to God alone, "who hath fashioned hearts one by one" ( Ps.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on John and Hebrews

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Kings 15:23
body: “What then," saith one, "do all diseases proceed from sin?" Not all, but most of them; and some proceed from different kinds of loose living, since gluttony, intemperance, and sloth, produce such like sufferings.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on John and Hebrews

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Kings 18:18
body: “Seest thou his courage? Behold also the courage of John the Baptist, which he used before Herod; when he said, "It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother Philip's wife." (Mark vi.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Kings 18:18
body: “And what could be poorer than Jacob (tell me), who said, "If the Lord give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on"?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on John and Hebrews

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Kings 19:10
body: “Next, tell me with what view were they to take such a course? They did not immediately, leaving Judæa, go into the Gentile cities, but went up and down within its limit.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Kings 19:10
body: “What then is one to say? That the Saints knew not all things. And this one might learn from many instances, both of the early ones, and of those who came after them, as Elisha knew not concerning the woman (2 Kings iv.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon
